rubric.why: A triple covalent bond is formed by sharing three pairs of electrons.
rubric.description: Describes how the triple bond forms.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the atoms share three pairs of electrons.

rubric.why: A nitrogen molecule is a standard example of a triple covalent bond.
rubric.how: Award for naming nitrogen (N₂) or showing its triple bond.

modelAnswer: A triple covalent bond is formed when two atoms share three pairs of electrons.
For example, two nitrogen atoms share three pairs of electrons to form N₂ (N≡N).

items.followUp: State one difference between polar and non-polar covalent bonds.

rubric.why: In a polar covalent bond, the shared electrons are unequally distributed between the atoms.
rubric.description: Describes electron sharing in a polar covalent bond.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the shared electrons are distributed unequally.

rubric.why: In a non-polar covalent bond, the shared electrons are equally distributed between the atoms.
rubric.description: Describes electron sharing in a non-polar covalent bond.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the shared electrons are distributed equally.

modelAnswer: In a polar covalent bond, the shared electrons are distributed unequally between the bonded atoms.
In a non-polar covalent bond, the shared electrons are distributed equally between the bonded atoms.

items.followUp: What happens to the rate of evaporation when the surface area of a liquid is increased?

rubric.why: A rise in temperature increases the rate of evaporation.
rubric.description: States the effect of temperature on evaporation.
rubric.how: Award for stating that higher temperature increases the rate of evaporation.

rubric.why: At a higher temperature, molecules have more kinetic energy and more can escape from the liquid's surface into the vapour.
rubric.description: Explains the effect in terms of particles.
rubric.how: Award for linking increased molecular kinetic energy with molecules escaping from the surface.

modelAnswer: As the temperature of a liquid increases, its rate of evaporation increases.
The molecules gain kinetic energy, so more molecules can escape from the liquid’s surface into the vapour.

items.followUp: How can boiling point be used to distinguish a pure solid from a mixture?

rubric.why: A pure liquid has a definite boiling point at a given pressure.
rubric.description: States the boiling behaviour of a pure liquid.
rubric.how: Award for identifying its fixed or definite boiling point.

rubric.why: A solution generally boils over a range of temperatures rather than at one fixed temperature.
rubric.description: States the boiling behaviour of a solution.
rubric.how: Award for stating that its boiling point is not fixed or that it boils over a range.

modelAnswer: A pure liquid has a fixed, definite boiling point at a given pressure.
A solution does not have a fixed boiling point and generally boils over a range of temperatures.
